claims.text: DFT+DMFT will predict finite local magnetic moments more reliably than standard LDA/GGA.
DFT+DMFT will stabilize ferromagnetic ground states more reliably than standard DFT.
A hybrid functional incorporating nonlocal exchange and spin-fluctuation corrections can serve as an equivalent alternative to DFT+DMFT for predicting ferromagnetic ground states.
Standard DFT tends to underestimate magnetic-moment formation in transition-metal compounds or semiconductors.
The underestimation by standard DFT results from its limited treatment of strong correlations and spin fluctuations.
The proposed framework explicitly includes dynamic local electron correlations and longitudinal spin fluctuations.
The proposed calculations are ground-state, zero-temperature calculations.
Enhanced treatment of local correlations and spin fluctuations modifies the electronic structure and stabilizes finite magnetic moments.
Stabilization of finite magnetic moments promotes ferromagnetic ordering.
DMFT captures strong local electron interactions and spin fluctuations that LDA/GGA miss.
Including these interactions lowers the total energy of ferromagnetic configurations relative to nonmagnetic or antiferromagnetic configurations.
The proposed method is expected to yield finite and sizable magnetic moments.
The proposed method is expected to predict a ferromagnetic ground state below competing magnetic orders in energy.
The proposed method will more accurately reflect the intrinsic ferromagnetism of the material.
LDA or GGA may predict a nonmagnetic or weakly magnetic ground state because of inadequate treatment of exchange-correlation effects and strong interactions.
The proposed method may be less accurate when nonlocal correlations or extreme electron correlations dominate.
The method's predictive power should be benchmarked against well-characterized experimental systems.
